clue.text: Sad time in prison? It flies!

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
bird is British slang for a prison sentence, from rhyming slang bird-lime = time

explanation.surface: A gloomy spell behind bars, with an exclamation that seems to cheer it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad time in prison?' reads as a single grim phrase, but it splits into two pieces; 'doing bird' is British slang for serving a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluebird is a small songbird, so it is something that flies.

clue.text: Druggie could cause riot inside

indicators.note: inside says the letters sit within the run of words cause riot

explanation.surface: An addict is the type who might start a disturbance in the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like prison slang, but it signals letters sitting within 'cause riot'; 'could' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is a slang term for a drug taker, so it means a druggie.

clue.text: A lawless thief: I was once one myself

definitions.text: A lawless thief: I was once one myself

parts.words: A lawless thief: I was once one myself
parts.note: a seagoing robber confessing a past career outside the law, as a reformed buccaneer might

explanation.surface: A reformed outlaw admits to a criminal past.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea who acts outside any law.

clue.text: You and I back film

parts.note: you and I together are we
the stern is the back part of a ship

explanation.surface: Two people declaring their support for a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like support or a reversal, but here it is a noun: the stern is the rear of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A western is a genre of film set in the American Old West.

clue.text: Floral tribute to the "Immortals"?

parts.note: a flower whose name in Greek means unfading, long a poetic emblem of things that never die

explanation.surface: A wreath laid in honour of the immortal gods or heroes.
explanation.definitionFit: The amaranth was a legendary never-fading flower, a traditional symbol of immortality.

clue.text: She runs the meeting I join in daily

indicators.note: join in says the letter I is slipped inside the word for a daily

parts.note: a daily is British for a cleaning woman who comes in each day, a charwoman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman presiding over a gathering, with someone joining each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'daily' looks like 'every day', but in British usage a daily is a cleaner, a charwoman; I goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A chairwoman is the woman who presides over and runs a meeting.

clue.text: Hooker upset prince

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of prince are jumbled

explanation.surface: A prostitute has distressed a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooker' suggests a prostitute or a rugby forward, but it is a claw that hooks; 'upset' rearranges PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pincer is a claw, as on a crab, which hooks and grips things.

clue.text: Fifth Beatle with special arrangement of Pepper?

indicators.note: an arrangement of letters puts them in a new order, so these are reshuffled
Fifth picks out the letter in fifth position of the word Beatle

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A nod to the 'fifth Beatle' and a fresh arrangement of Sgt Pepper.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Beatles' Sgt Pepper album; L (fifth letter of BEATLE) joins SPECIAL and 'arrangement of' rearranges them all.
explanation.definitionFit: Allspice is also called Jamaica pepper, the dried berry of a Caribbean tree used as a spice.

clue.text: First two pieces of Mozart's musical material

indicators.note: the first two pieces of the word Mozart's are its opening pair of letters

parts.note: Hair is the famous 1960s rock musical

explanation.surface: The opening bars of a Mozart composition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musical' looks like an adjective describing material, but it is a noun: the stage show Hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Mohair is a fabric or yarn made from Angora goat hair, a kind of material.

clue.text: King Edward?

definitions.meaning: King ... is the title monarch of Shakespeare's tragedy
Edward ... was the Victorian nonsense poet, the question mark flagging an example

explanation.surface: Is this a monarch called Edward?
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward suggests an English monarch (or a potato), but the clue splits: a Shakespeare king and the poet Edward of that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic king and the nonsense poet Edward share this surname.

clue.text: Poor Clare gets pieta as a church adornment

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters of the two words are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A nun of the Poor Clares receives a sculpture of the Virgin with Christ to decorate the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Clares are an order of nuns, so 'Poor' seems part of a name; it is the anagram signal for CLARE + PIETA.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is a painting or carving placed behind an altar to decorate a church.

clue.text: The last appearance of the RAF in Alexandria

indicators.note: of says the letters are taken out of the run RAF in Alexandria

explanation.surface: Air force personnel make a final showing in the Egyptian city.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'rAF IN ALExandria', signalled by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A finale is the closing number or final appearance of a show.

clue.text: An unruly lot that won't take orders

definitions.text: An unruly lot that won't take orders

parts.words: An unruly lot that won't take orders
parts.note: a disorderly group who reject all authority, with orders read as commands rather than holy orders

explanation.surface: A rowdy crowd who refuse instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Anarchists reject government and authority, refusing to obey commands.

clue.text: Skin problem got from a disgusting boxer?

definitions.text: Skin problem got from a disgusting boxer?

parts.words: Skin problem got from a disgusting boxer?
parts.note: a fungal skin infection pictured as caught from a repulsive creature in the boxing arena

explanation.surface: A fighter so revolting that his opponents catch a rash.
explanation.walkthrough: A boxer fights in a ring, and a worm is a contemptible person: a 'worm of the ring'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringworm is a contagious fungal infection causing round red patches on the skin.

clue.text: Early promotion

definitions.meaning: in ..., as in a payment made beforehand
a step up in rank, a move forward

explanation.surface: Someone moved up the ladder ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An advance is both something given ahead of time and a forward step in rank.

clue.text: Jesus fellowships at Oxford and Cambridge

definitions.text: Jesus fellowships at Oxford and Cambridge

parts.words: Jesus fellowships at Oxford and Cambridge
parts.note: both ancient universities have a body named after Jesus, each a society of fellows

explanation.surface: Religious brotherhoods at the two oldest English universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jesus fellowships' suggests Christian groups, but Jesus College exists at both Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxford and Cambridge are made up of self-governing communities of fellows, each named like Jesus.

clue.text: "Church Times", unusual source of drugs

indicators.note: unusual means out of the ordinary form, so the letters of times are rearranged

explanation.surface: The religious newspaper as an odd place to find narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Times is a real Anglican weekly newspaper, so the quotation marks make the two words look like one title; 'unusual' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is the British term for a pharmacy, where medicines are dispensed.

clue.text: Times for sitting in judgement

parts.note: periods when a court or magistrates sit to hear cases

explanation.surface: The hours when a court is in operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Court sessions are the periods during which judges sit to try cases.

clue.text: Judges found at play

parts.note: people who assess a performance, seated in the audience of a theatre production

explanation.surface: Magistrates caught having fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' suggests the bench and 'at play' suggests leisure, but these are reviewers watching a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Critics judge and review works such as theatre productions.

clue.text: Stern pedant's cane

parts.note: a strict, fussy person pictured as one who wields a rod

explanation.surface: The stick carried by a severe schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: A pedant who insists on rules is a word built on STICK, so the cane joke links the person to the rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler is someone who insists rigidly on rules or detail, a strict pedant.

clue.text: Did this Tommy wear his best bib?

definitions.text: Did this Tommy wear his best bib?

parts.words: Did this Tommy wear his best bib?
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme boy who sang for his supper, plus the phrase best bib and ..., meaning one's finest clothes

explanation.surface: Asking whether a boy put on his smartest clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Tommy ___ is a nursery-rhyme character, and 'best bib and ___' is an old idiom for one's finest outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the nursery-rhyme Tommy is also the lace collar in the phrase about best clothes.

clue.text: The texture of curtains

definitions.meaning: the surface quality or texture of a material, as a glossy coating
curtains is slang for the end, as in it's curtains for him

explanation.surface: Asking about the feel of the fabric used for drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtains' looks like drapes, matching texture, but it is slang for the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is a surface texture, and also the end of something.

clue.text: Mate — Robin was a good one

definitions.meaning: Robin Goodfellow is another name for the mischievous sprite Puck

explanation.surface: A friend says Robin was decent company.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is the English folklore sprite, Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a companion, and Puck's other name is Robin Good-plus-this.

clue.text: It could be a sharp chance

definitions.meaning: in music notation a sharp, flat or natural sign added before a note

explanation.surface: A clever stroke of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sharp' suggests clever, but it is the musical sign; the question frames a sharp as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: An accidental is a sign altering a note's pitch, and accidental also means happening by luck.

clue.text: Mariners can do it without one

definitions.text: Mariners can do it without one

parts.words: Mariners can do it without one
parts.note: seafarers can travel the water with no canvas at all, using engines or oars, the verb and noun forms of one word

explanation.surface: Seamen can manage the job without a particular piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb and the noun are the same word: sailors can voyage without the canvas sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to voyage by boat, and a sail is the canvas sheet catching the wind.

clue.text: Window frame is half wood

indicators.note: half of the two-letter word is means one of its two letters, here the second

parts.note: ash is a hardwood timber from the ash tree

explanation.surface: A window frame made half of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' takes the second half of 'is', giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the sliding frame holding the glass in a sash window.

clue.text: Quiet resolve

definitions.meaning: to calm or soothe, as when settling a baby
to sort out a dispute or matter

explanation.surface: A calm determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolve' looks like a noun meaning determination, but it is a verb meaning sort out.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle is both to calm someone down and to resolve a dispute.

clue.text: Annoying a pelican, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a pelican is a type of British pedestrian street ... with traffic lights, the perhaps marking an example

explanation.surface: An irritating seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: A pelican crossing is a British pedestrian crossing controlled by push-button traffic lights; 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossing someone is thwarting them, and a pelican is one type of street crossing.
